rewrites.comment: The signed-in console is a single-page app. Every /app/** URL serves the PRE-RENDERED CONSOLE SHELL, not the home page: the shell's static HTML is the splash the AuthProvider shows while it resolves the first ID token, so a deep link hydrates into a loading state rather than flashing the marketing home page and then replacing it.

headers.comment: Fingerprinted build assets are immutable: the filename changes whenever the bytes do, so they can be cached for a year. Fonts are served from the same origin and need the CORS header because they are fetched with crossorigin (a preload requirement).
HTML is never cached at the edge for long: a release must reach visitors immediately, and the HTML is small. must-revalidate forces a conditional request rather than a stale render.

Baseline security headers. The ENFORCING Content-Security-Policy is not here: it is stamped into every built page as a <meta http-equiv> by scripts/csp-hashes.mjs (run by npm run build), because its script-src lists the sha256 of each page's own inline scripts (the index.html theme bootstrap, plus vite-react-ssg's __staticRouterHydrationData and __VITE_REACT_SSG_HASH__, which vary per route and per build) and no single header can. That script is the one place the policy and its third-party allow-list (Firebase, App Check's reCAPTCHA, Google sign-in, Stripe, Mapbox) are defined; any new origin is added there. A meta policy cannot carry frame-ancestors, so it is sent here as the only header-borne CSP, and the browser enforces both. HSTS is not set here because Firebase Hosting already sends it on both its own and custom domains.
